quest.title: Like a Triumphant Hero
quest.description: It has been a long time since the Sabzeruz samsara, and many things cannot be ascertained until Nahida gets back in form. Today, you go to the Adventurers' Guild as usual...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x900, Mora x36000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Talk to Katheryne in Sumeru City

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Ad astra abyssosque! We meet again, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi Katheryne, do you have any commissions for us today?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Commissions, huh? Hmmm, let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Oh, how about this? Please attend the Akademiya's academic symposium this afternoon, and recite a love poem onstage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, wait, say what now?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: And if possible, please also use your Kamera to capture the reaction of the audience upon finishing the poem.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What kind of commission is that?

choices.text: I feel embarrassed just imagining it.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: I see... It appears that you're not interested in this commission.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: In that case, please go to Port Ormos and convince the Eremites there to spend some time volunteering at the local orphanage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! That's not any better!

choices.text: Isn't that just asking for a beating?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Mm-hmm, I'm sure the mercenaries will have some interesting reactions as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Paimon's gotta ask... Just who exactly has been submitting these commissions to the Adventurers' Guild?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Oh, the commissioner? Hmm, well actually, I just wanted to see the two of you in action...

choices.text: You're not actually Katheryne, are you?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hehe, was it so obvious? I was hoping you would actually take one of those commissions. That kind of chance to observe humans doesn't come by often...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh, so it's Nahida! Paimon just knew Katheryne wouldn't crack those kinds of jokes. When did you get into her head?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm... From when she said "Ad astra abyssosque"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So it's been you this whole time!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Are you done resting up, Nahida?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes. I've been sleeping ever since we parted ways, and I even had a really, really long dream...

choices.text: So, the Akasha can't take away the dreams of gods?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It was another dream about the Sabzeruz Festival, except it was a happy one!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: In my dream, I was sitting in the middle of a flower terrace, and everyone in Sumeru City was holding hands as they danced in circles around me... They danced round and round, and everyone looked really happy.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I also got to sit on a gigantic flower carriage. Farris, the Knight of Flowers, raised me really, really high above the ground, and I was throwing an endless amount of Yalda Candies at the children...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know, Nahida, maybe your dream is how the Sabzeruz Festival really should be. It's meant to be a joyous time, where everyone gets together to celebrate your birthday...

choices.text: Yeah...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Eh? Wasn't I describing a really happy dream? Why are you both looking at me like that... Wait, could this be an example of the emotion known as "pity"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, we aren't pitying you! That would only make everything worse. We just don't want you to feel too sad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, have you had a chance to visit Dunyarzad? How's she doing? The Homayanis haven't allowed any visitors after the festival, so we haven't been able to check on her.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, I paid her a visit right after I woke up. She was resting at the time.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Her condition has stabilized. However, since Eleazar is a manifestation of the Withering on the human body, we can only cure it by finding a way to take care of Irminsul's own withering.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But for the moment, our top focus should still be figuring out what the sages are up to and what they're planning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right. Who knows what'll happen if they manage to pull off another scheme like the samsara of the Sabzeruz Festival.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So, our first priority should be investigating and putting a stop to the sages' activities. As for how we should pull that off, let's discuss it somewhere else. There are too many adventurers around here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, good point! Uh, sorry adventurers, we're gonna be borrowing Katheryne for a little while~!

choices.text: But in reality...
What did you dream about?
You're Nahida, right?
Mercenaries and orphanages really don't go together.
The audience would definitely have a... reaction.

talks.objective: Continue talking to Nahida somewhere else

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't think of anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Are we really out of ideas?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida, you're super smart, so you already have something in mind, right? Don't keep us in suspense — spill the beans already!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: According to a popular theory from the Vahumana Darshan of the Akademiya, rejecting impractical motions at the beginning of a planning session will give more weight to the actual proposal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, but aren't you the God of Wisdom? You don't have to use that kind of gimmick to make us take your ideas seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well, I've been thinking that if I can't directly possess the leaders, and if I can't get ordinary people involved...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Then I should find someone who's already involved, but hasn't decided to side with the sages.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're saying we should recruit a spy? Hmm, that does sound like it could work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Before coming back, we met someone named Alhaitham. He seems like he acts alone, and he likes doing stuff behind the Akademiya's back. They probably aren't in cahoots.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Actually, I already have someone in mind. Do you still remember that female scholar named Setaria?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Setaria... Paimon remembers now! Isn't she the one who's always trailing behind the Grand Sage of the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We ran into her basically every time the Sabzeruz Festival repeated itself. You could even say we're old enemies by now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon still remembers the smug and mean way she always spoke to Nilou!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. I've always liked observing all kinds of people, and Setaria has always stood out from the crowd.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: She was born in the desert, and was hailed as their greatest genius. Her academic gifts allowed her special admission into the Akademiya, and also gave her the opportunity to serve as the sages' assistant.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon didn't know she was from the desert! She must be pretty special, then. Paimon feels like most of the desert-dwellers around the city are working as mercenaries.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The name Setaria means "star." When she lived in the desert, she shone like the brightest star in the night sky.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Later on, she was chosen by the Sun. The star was given a place in the daytime sky to complement the Sun's dazzling light.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Soon after, the star witnessed the Sun scorching the earth, which brought forth many disasters.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The star began to waver. Instead of staying beside such a sun, wouldn't it be better to return and light up part of the night sky?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But in the end, she couldn't give up the radiance of daytime. To cope with her shame, the star buried her guilt and closed her eyes...

choices.text: This is no longer just a metaphor...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From the sound of it, Setaria's just hung up on the research opportunities here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But she doesn't really support the Akademiya. She still feels guilty about not doing more for the desert, right...? She's just running away from her problems!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Indeed. When they are presented with complex moral issues, many people will simply plug their ears and go with the flow until the problem can't be fixed anymore.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: She's suppressing a lot of guilt, but before she realized it, she had already become the sages' accomplice. She can't deny her part in their schemes anymore.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds exactly like the person we need.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Right. We must somehow make her face her problems again...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That way, not only can we get useful intel from her, but she can also use it as an opportunity to redeem herself.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: From my past observations, Setaria will take a day off from the Akademiya every ten days to do some shopping in the city.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Tomorrow afternoon just happens to be a shopping day for her. That'll be our chance.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: To prepare, let's go check out some of her favorite spots, and have a quick chat with a few of the vendors there.

choices.text: Those are Setaria's true thoughts, right?

talks.objective: Gather information as instructed by Nahida

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This should be Setaria's favorite fortune-telling spot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... so, should we ask the fortune-teller about Setaria?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: No, I already have enough information on Setaria. The most important thing now is for you to pay attention to the vendor's talking style and key characteristics.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Talking style and... key characteristics?

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: My poor lost lambs, have you become troubled over your fates?

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: The divine voice of wisdom often echoes between mine ears. If thou be blessed today by the gods, I may be able to show you the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, really? Nahida, you've been whispering things to her?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Shh... Ahem, my friend here has some doubts regarding {F#her}{M#his} future. Can we get a fortune reading for {F#her}{M#him}?

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: Hummm... of course, of course. In that case...

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya's Cat
dialogues.text: Meow!

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: Oho, it would seem that Harut and Marut are quite wary of you. Perhaps at some time in the past, you have somehow offended the gods?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Only mocking the God of Anemo, questioning the Lord of Geo's financial savviness, and brawling with the God of Electro... Do those count?

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Oh, nothing. {NICKNAME}, go on, pick an aspect for her to divine.

choices.text: Divine my prospects in health.

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Health prospects? No problem at all.

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Hummm... The gods have spoken. The truth shall be revealed.

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Your life shall continue on for... for... Huh!? Many... many tens of thousands of years!? Impossible...

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Harut, Marut, did you two spoil my divination? I've never read a fortune so absurd.

response.speaker: Cat
response.text: Meow?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, actually, Paimon thinks this is probably the most accurate fortune-telling you've ever done...

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Ahem, I admit that the orientation of today's celestial matrix is suboptimal. As such, there will be no charge.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Is that so... Well, that can't be helped.

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: If you were to bring some food offerings for Harut and Marut on your next visit, perhaps they could help you reverse the wheels of fate?

choices.text: Divine my prospects in love.

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Love prospects? No problem at all.

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Hummm... The gods have spoken. The truth shall be revealed.

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: One who is fated to cross your path will appear on... on... Huh!? So... so many people will fall for you!? How could that be...

talks.objective: Gather information as instructed by Nahida

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this another one of Setaria's favorite stalls?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yep. It belongs to Akim. His father helped Setaria a lot when she first moved to Sumeru City, so she still comes by whenever she has time.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: When I start talking with him, listen carefully to the details of our conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: Ah, dear customers, would you like to look at some pottery?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We caught wind of your great craftsmanship, so we specifically came to take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: Oh! I recognize you. Aren't you Miss Katheryne from the Adventurers' Guild? Sounds like I'm in for some big business!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Speaking of, where did you learn this trade?

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: I suppose you could say it all started with my dad. He's a mason by trade, but I picked up an interest in clay while apprenticing for him.

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: After that, I began making pottery by myself in secret, and I simply changed trades when my works turned out well. Although, it's a pity that I'm no longer making much use of the knowledge provided to me by the Akasha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's nice! You're making a living doing something you love!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hmm, so is your father still working as a mason?

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: Oh no, not anymore. A few years back, he fell from a roof and broke his leg. Since he had already saved enough Mora over all these years, he's just enjoying the retired life in Port Ormos nowadays.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I see. We wish him peace and happiness in his retirement.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'll have someone in charge of logistics at the guild come by another day for some goods. We'll leave you to it. Take care now!

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: No problem. Rest easy, all our goods are sure to meet your every need.

talks.objective: Gather information as instructed by Nahida

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This should be our final stop. Setaria is always thinking of this restaurant when she's working at the Akademiya, so she always comes by whenever she's out in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida, you've really thought of everything!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's my duty to protect Sumeru's citizens, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hi there. I feel like I've seen you down by the docks before...

dialogues.speaker: Qishan
dialogues.text: Huh? Sorry, I don't quite remember...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: If I recall, you were having a discussion with someone about ship-building at the time.

dialogues.speaker: Qishan
dialogues.text: Ah, that's right! I've always been really interested in feats of marine engineering.

dialogues.speaker: Qishan
dialogues.text: After all, I grew up in Liyue Harbor and spent my entire childhood staring at the ships going in and out of the port. I came to Sumeru to study, but failed to make it into the Akademiya due to my lack of talent.

dialogues.speaker: Qishan
dialogues.text: But I'm still discussing all kinds of problems with different scholars, and I'm continuing to study and perform research from the restaurant's basement. I'm sure I'll get into the Akademiya after their next round of exams!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: What an admirable spirit for learning. Amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure... But you'll find hard-working people wherever you go!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So this restaurant has a basement as well? Huh, first I've heard of it.

dialogues.speaker: Qishan
dialogues.text: That's right! It's not usually open to patrons. Most of the time, employees use it for breaks or to hold private events.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I see... Guess that makes sense. Well, good luck with your studies, Miss Qishan.

dialogues.speaker: Qishan
dialogues.text: Haha, thank you so much. As long as I can make it into the Akademiya as an official student, I'll be happy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, was that everybody?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. Three familiar faces should be enough for Setaria.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the point of all the information we've collected? Nahida, you still haven't told us how you're planning to make Setaria face her problems.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Setaria is already used to avoiding her problems, so we must find a way to break through her usual sensibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I remember you mentioned that the Eremites in Port Ormos are all making a fuss about the upcoming resurrection of King Deshret.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Although it's all just a boatload of nonsense, the faith of her homeland may turn out to be Setaria's soft spot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it now... You want to take advantage of the guilt Setaria feels about her homeland.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although she knows she should return home to help the people of the desert, all she's done is conspire with the sages...

choices.text: If King Deshret were to criticize Setaria's actions...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, so how do we set that up?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Well, King Deshret is long gone, and Setaria is also too smart to fall for any simple tricks...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If we simply engaged her under the guise of King Deshret's believers, she'd definitely be wary of us, and we may not get anywhere.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But if we were to "borrow" some of her close acquaintances to talk with her... her reaction would probably be very different.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you mean, you're going to possess those people we just talked to?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yep. Possess them through the Akasha, imply that they've already converted to the faith of King Deshret, and then convey our made-up "will of King Deshret."

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: As long as everything goes smoothly, we'll get through to Setaria for sure. She'll never guess that we had anything to do with it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh, so that's how you're going to use all the info we collected on these people — it's so that you won't slip up and break form! Possessing them will only work if you can manage to pass off as them.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Exactly! So, best of luck with impersonating them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Best of luck? B—But we don't know how to possess anyone!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's no problem at all. I'll just share all their senses with you once I've possessed them. As long as you're also wearing an Akasha Terminal, the effect will basically be as if you've possessed them yourself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh, that is pretty convenient... But why does {F#she}{M#he} have to do this? Can't you do it yourself?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Although I've been observing humans for a while, I've never been good at imitating them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, you're not wrong... It's always been painfully obvious whenever you try to pass as Katheryne.

choices.text: Alright.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: *sigh* If it was at all possible, I would've preferred to leave these people alone, but seeing how things are now, I probably should just accept it and push on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, don't beat yourself up over it! We're only doing this to help everyone, and we'll only be borrowing them for a little while anyway.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Alright, then let's give it a go tomorrow afternoon.

choices.text: I'll try my best.
If King Deshret were to make demands of Setaria...

talks.objective: Go to the market and carry out Nahida's plan

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, here she comes! Setaria's here!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Let's quietly follow her. Once she starts talking to her acquaintances, we'll find a safe spot to begin possessing them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #As for how we'll sway her to our side... I'll leave that to you. {NICKNAME}, I trust you'll know what to say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh, Paimon's starting to feel kinda nervous! Okay, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like they've already started talking... Let's find a hiding spot and get started!

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: ...That's right, you really can't force anything when it comes to love. And besides, everyone around me has a very different background and outlook...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you still listening to me, Nabiya?

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: Oh, o—of course I'm listening! You were talking about troubles with your love life, right? I heard everything you said.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Ah, okay then. You just seemed a little distracted for a moment there.

dialogues.speaker: Cat
dialogues.text: Meow!

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Strange... Your cats seem pretty worked up. Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: I always thought they were quiet, happy kitties... Oh, what are their names again?

choices.text: Hamru and Tamru.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Hmm, are you sure? Those aren't ringing a bell for some reason...

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Ah, well... A—Actually, they have many names. Which names I use depends on my mood.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Huh, I see. I imagine that must be hard for the kitties, too.

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Ahem, so which fortune do you want me to read for you today? You must have come for another echo of the divine voice of wisdom.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Hmm... I'd like to get another reading on my love prospects, but to be perfectly honest with you, I feel like I've been a real mess recently...

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: A mess?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Well, erm... Could you do a reading on how long it'll take me to finish my current project at work? I really just want to get it over with...

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: I hear you... No problem at all. Uh, the gods will reveal the truth.

choices.text: Hummm... Ah, the gods have spoken!

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: The gods are asking...

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: "Setaria, why haven't you gone home?"

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Why haven't I gone... home? Do the gods really know everything I've been thinking about...?

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: "Setaria, why don't you just go home!" It's a demand now, instead of a question... The gods seem to be truly upset.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Ah! Ah... I'm sorry, I know I failed the gods. Please pass on my most sincere apologies and ask for their divine forgiveness...

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: And, if I may ask... Nabiya, is there a specific god who's speaking to you right now?

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Hmph, what an inconsiderate and naive question. The god who is speaking to me is, of course, the wisest and mightiest of all: King Deshret.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: K—King Deshret? No wonder he would make such a demand of me... Huh, wait a second... King Deshret passed away a long time ago...

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Even though news of King Deshret's resurrection has been spreading like wildfire, it's all just a misinformation campaign from the Akademiya... How can King Deshret still exist in real life?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh? King Deshret's resurrection is a misinformation campaign?)

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: What insolence! I am King Deshret's most loyal believer. Do you wish to refute his voice of wisdom?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Oh, no, no... As a child of the desert, I am only reveling in his power upon learning that his divine glory has touched even this city.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: I will think very carefully about his demand of me... I'm sorry, I must go now.

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Ah, wait...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, she just ran off in a hurry. She looked pretty upset, too!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #Well done, {NICKNAME}! Setaria didn't seem to suspect anything amiss.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: To have something she's been trying desperately to avoid show up out of nowhere and berate her... That must have shaken her to the core.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida, it seems like you understand human emotions really well after all!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: All I know are some abstract Haravatat theories. In any case, my time with you has shown a lot of them to be utterly useless. I'm still trying to make sense of everything...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Anyway, enough of that. Let's hurry and catch up to Setaria.

choices.text: Ohohoho... The gods have spoken!

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Pfft... Sorry, your new laugh is just so hilarious, I couldn't help it...

response.speaker: Nabiya
response.text: Oh! Uh, please pay no mind to those kinds of details.

choices.text: Harut and Marut.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Ahh, that's right! They are just little darlings, aren't they? Harut and Marut...

talks.objective: Wait for Nahida to enter the inhabitant's consciousness and talk to Setaria

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: ...It's okay, I just got caught up in something.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Oh, actually, didn't you ask me to help you look for work? What kind of work were you looking for again?

choices.text: Uh, gardening work.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Gardening? But don't you hate everything to do with plants? I still remember getting mad at you for secretly throwing away the bonsai that I gave you as a present.

response.speaker: Akim
response.text: Erm... Well, uh, you see, a friend told me that the secret to self-improvement is to work on things you're not so good at.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: ...Fair enough. I didn't think that was something you would consider.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Speaking of, how's he doing? Is he feeling any better?

choices.text: He's feeling a lot better, and he's walking more now.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Ah, that's good to hear. I've been thinking a lot about him... If I could get some more time off, I'd love to pay him a visit.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Actually, while we're talking about him... Is he still living in Port Ormos?

response.speaker: Akim
response.text: Yeah, he's been retired there for a while.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: If you could find the time, please write him a letter. Let him know that recently, faith in King Deshret has taken root in Port Ormos, and has begun to spread across Sumeru...

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: He has a quick temper, and has always been a devout follower of the Dendro Archon... I don't want him to get into a fight with those King Deshret believers because of a difference in beliefs.

response.speaker: Akim
response.text: Oh? So who are you siding with in all of this? The Akademiya or King Deshret?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Uh, I...

response.speaker: Akim
response.text: *sigh* I'm so jealous of you — you were born a child of the desert. Yet, you chose to betray King Deshret, and now you spend all your time with those crooks from the Akademiya...

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Akim...? You don't mean... You've also become a believer of King Deshret?

response.speaker: Akim
response.text: What's so strange about becoming a believer of the wise King Deshret? In fact, aren't you the strange one — the one who still can't pick a side?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: C—Can't pick a side... Me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whoa, {NICKNAME}! Paimon had no idea you'd be so good at this.

choices.text: Before I knew it, I really started getting into the role.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You really zeroed in on the issue and put it right in front of her. It might feel a bit overwhelming for Setaria...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But once everything is over, I'll be sure to pay a visit to her mind and explain everything. Anyway, let's keep going.

choices.text: I wasn't too harsh, was I?
He's feeling a lot better. He can lift stuff now.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Huh? Wasn't he nursing a leg injury? If I recall correctly, his strong arms had always been his pride and joy.

response.speaker: Akim
response.text: Uhh, he... sprained his arm a while back while trying to show off his strength. I thought you'd heard.

choices.text: Uh, masonry work.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Oh, right, your old man's craft... How could I forget?

talks.objective: Wait for Nahida to enter the inhabitant's consciousness and talk to Setaria

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: ...So, Qishan, have you noticed anything weird in the city lately?

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: Like... as if someone was trying to preach to you about something.

choices.text: No, I've been spending all my time studying in the basement.

response.speaker: Qishan
response.text: Oh right, speaking of strange things...

response.speaker: Qishan
response.text: I celebrated the Sabzeruz Festival so many times that I lost count. That was really weird.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Wait, how could you be aware of that!? That should be impossible. Nothing in the report indicated anything like that...

response.speaker: Qishan
response.text: Are you still failing to realize that the Akademiya's lowly tricks could never deceive all of Sumeru's citizens?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: ...Qishan, don't tell me that you've converted to King Deshret as well?

response.speaker: Qishan
response.text: What an absurd question. You make it sound like I should be ashamed for becoming a believer of King Deshret.

response.speaker: Qishan
response.text: In reality, shouldn't you be the one who is ashamed? You, who worked side-by-side with the Akademiya and treated people as nothing more than experimental subjects?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Please... Please stop!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even now, Setaria's still trying to run from her problems...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did I push too hard?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: She can no longer justify everything to herself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, she's trying to talk to the guards! What should we do?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This is the most important part of all. Quick, get ready!

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: ...Mercenary, you're a member of the Corps of Thirty, correct? Please help me pass a message to the matra right away. The situation in the city is getting out of control...

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: Please, try to remain calm, miss. Tell me, what's happening in the city?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Heretics are infiltrating the city, and they've already converted many residents to their side...

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: Heretics? What kind of heresy are you talking about?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: King Deshret! Many people I know have suddenly started believing in him, but he's long dead... It's impossible...

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: Miss Setaria... Nothing is impossible.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Y—You know my name?

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: King Deshret is immortal, and all who defy him will one day pay the price.

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: You must face the truth, Setaria. You tread a treacherous path, and the longer you ignore it, the tighter the Akademiya's grasp on you will become, and the deeper you will be ensnared.

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: Child of King Deshret, never forget that the desert that belongs to you lies elsewhere.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: *sigh* ...It seems that no matter where I run, I only keep finding more believers of King Deshret. I have to say, this is a familiar feeling...

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: I've also been running from my guilt this whole time... Guilt over my part in the sages' plans, and from ignoring the letters from the children of my homeland.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: But no matter how much I may try to ignore or get rid of it, my guilt always comes back.

choices.text: You should follow your heart.

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: You won't necessarily lose your research opportunities by facing the truth. Besides, did you really want to conduct your research while carrying such heavy feelings of guilt?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: How do you know me so well? Are you truly just a believer of King Deshret, or are you the god himself?

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: That's not important. The important thing is to pass judgment on the Akademiya and its sages, and to correct their mistakes.

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: If you could provide some assistance in this matter, perhaps it could serve as a form of atonement.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: I've actually never believed in the gods, but I've always believed in serendipity. Your appearance must be a fated opportunity for me to get out of this wretched situation.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Please tell me... What can I do for you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Great, we've finally convinced her.)

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: Ahem... How much do you know about the sages' current activities?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: I was just one of the designers for the Mass Dream Harvest scheme... which is what happened around the Sabzeruz Festival.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: But I know very little about the full scope of the overall project. I'd assume that only staff with the highest clearance would have access to those confidential documents...

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: I've just been working to meet the Grand Sage's specified requirements.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: However, there's something that's been really bothering me... I heard that a scholar who was previously expelled has returned to the city, and even the sages are still quite wary of him...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (An outcast that even the sages are still wary of?)

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: To fight against the Akademiya, we will need to figure out the nature and the purpose of their work. Is there a way for us to get access to the confidential documents you mentioned?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: It should be possible if we're willing to take some risks. After all, I'm an assistant to the Grand Sage, and I've been working on many tasks outside of the project.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: One thing, though... I won't be able to transfer the documents to you through the Akasha once I get my hands on them. The sages have always closely monitored all activities within the Akasha.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Hmm, let me see... Let's use the most primitive method. Send someone to pick up the documents tomorrow evening at the Akademiya entrance.

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: The Akademiya entrance... Wouldn't that be too conspicuous?

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Don't worry about that. I assure you, this won't be a trap.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: I'm only suggesting this location because it'll draw more scrutiny for me to leave the Akademiya again. It'll be safest for me to distract the guards long enough to hand you the documents.

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: Alright, I trust you.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: So... If I were to successfully complete this task, would it mean I've atoned for my wrongdoings?

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: Umm... That'll depend on the judgment of the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: The Dendro Archon... That's right, her people are the ones we have endangered. As the God of Wisdom, she's also the one responsible for judging and guiding the scholars.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: ...Maybe it's time for me to find a god to believe in.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just as Nahida predicted, we've managed to bring Setaria to our side...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s execution was ingenious. {F#She}{M#He}'s the one who deserves all the praise.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Well, now that we've made plans to meet again tomorrow evening, all we can do is pray for Setaria's mission to go off without a hitch.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pray? But if we're going to pray to the gods, aren't we just praying to you, God of Wisdom and guardian of the scholars?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Me? No, no. The truth is the true guardian of scholars — I've always believed that. Anyway, let's meet again tomorrow evening at the Adventurers' Guild.

choices.text: It's not too late to turn back.
No, I've been spending all my time studying in the attic.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Wait, did you just say attic? I thought this place didn't have an attic... Also, don't you usually study in the basement?

response.speaker: Qishan
response.text: Uh, well... The restaurant recently added an attic. I've been studying there because it has better lighting.

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: I've never seen Harut and Marut be so wary of anyone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Katheryne, we're here! Oh, hmm... You're the "other" Katheryne, right?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's right. I suppose I'm the "other Katheryne" in your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can't we just call her Nahida?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shh...! We're on a secret mission tonight, so we need to protect Katheryne's identity!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yep, Paimon's right. We cannot fully rule out the chance that the meet-up tonight is just a trap.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: If something were to happen, my existence may be the only trump card we'll be able to play.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: After all, the Akademiya should still be unable to confirm the existence of my consciousness in the outside world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, yep! Exactly, just what Paimon was thinking!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I somehow doubt that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Anyway, enough about that! Let's just make sure to be on our guard!

choices.text: Speaking of which...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Off? What do you feel is off?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's just a little too quiet around here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's the middle of the night — of course it's quiet! You're not getting paranoid, are you?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #No, I think {NICKNAME}'s right. It really is a lot quieter than usual.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If you look around, there seems to be fewer people on the streets. I'm not sure if this is the case for the entire city, though...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, maybe it's just a coincidence? Maybe Setaria figured out a way to not only distract the guards, but also to get everyone to go to sleep early, just so we can exchange the documents in peace.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I also can't quite figure out why things feel a little off... But, now that we're here, let's go ahead and meet her as we planned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, regardless... as long as you're here with us, Paimon feels a little safer!

choices.text: Don't you feel like something is off?

talks.objective: Sort out the information you have

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be far enough... Phew, Paimon needs to catch her breath first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is Nahida going to be okay? We only made it out because of her...

choices.text: She can jump between minds. Hopefully she'll be fine?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wasn't counting on running into a new Harbinger here, let alone such a high-ranking one! That guy was number two... so scary...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He called himself "The Doctor"... Remember Tighnari told us about him. Setaria did say that someone who once got expelled from the Akademiya came back recently...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...and that even the sages are wary of him. Yep, sounds like she must've been talking about The Doctor.

choices.text: We underestimated the scale of this problem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Now that The Doctor's in the picture, we're no longer just dealing with the Akademiya — they're in cahoots with the Fatui.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what are the Fatui after this time? Another Gnosis?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We need to find a way to reunite with Nahida.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, things would be a lot easier with Nahida's help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida said "We'll meet again outside of the city," but we can't just keep waiting around, right?

choices.text: Let's start our own investigation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You mean...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go find Tighnari.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Right, wasn't he invited by the sages to work on some project when we were staying with him in the Avidya Forest? That has to be the same project.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though he turned it down at that time, he might still know something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no time to lose. Let's go to Gandharva Ville!

choices.text: Let's go find someone else who might be involved.
We underestimated the number of parties involved.
I'm not sure... that guy was pretty terrifying.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Let's continue our chat here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay. So do you have any ideas on how we can investigate the sages, Nahida?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Actually, I've already done a little bit of work on that, but for now, I want to hear your thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Possess a key figure in the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I've already tried that, but all the key members of the Akademiya — even the Corps of Thirty guards — intentionally avoid wearing their Akasha Terminals.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It seems that from the very beginning, they've been guarding against info leaks from the Akasha. Of course, it could also be because they're wary of me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you already caught the sages' attention?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm guessing not yet, but distrusting me would make perfect sense if they ever paid attention to the urban legends about me.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In any case, I probably can't take over their minds directly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Possess a student and infiltrate the sages' quarters?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: No way. That's too risky.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean it'd be too easy to get caught?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: No, it's not that. We shouldn't involve innocent students in this. A single mistake could completely ruin their lives.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Doing that would be ignoring the safety of my people for my own selfish goals. How is that any different from what the sages are doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a good point. Spoken like the God of Sumeru!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We could grab someone close to the sages and question them?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We're in the dark as of now. Since we still don't know anything about their goals, any rash move could tip them off and lead to terrible consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: After all, every person in Sumeru City is one of their hostages.

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: That was my first time talking with Miss Katheryne. Hehe, I'm sure I sounded a bit nervous...

dialogues.speaker: Qishan
dialogues.text: I must have met her somewhere. Why can't I remember?

dialogues.speaker: Nabiya
dialogues.text: Huh? What's gotten into Harut and Marut? They seem terrified of me all of a sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: Whoa... What happened just now? Wasn't I talking with Setaria? Where'd she go?

dialogues.speaker: Qishan
dialogues.text: *yawn* I seem to have dozed off just now... Maybe I studied way too late last night? Ah, I'm sorry, can I help you with anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've spent quite some time in Sumeru City, but ever since we last said goodbye to Lesser Lord Kusanali, we haven't heard anything from her...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* We can't just keep waiting around like this. Let's go find Katheryne and pick up some work so we can at least keep ourselves busy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's at Akim's now, right on cue! Let's get ready to possess him right away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #C'mon {NICKNAME}! Setaria's already started talking with Qishan!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, there really aren't many people out right now... Let's hope it'll be this quiet in front of the Akademiya, and that Setaria managed to distract all the guards...
